text:
marta: FYI new report from a customer: their bulk paginate+embed job stalls intermittently when using the Go SDK but runs fine with JS.
tom: Any error logs? stack traces?
marta: Only symptoms: stuck at "fetching page 3" for 40s, then resumes. No 5xx from API, but we see many client-side queued goroutines. Paste from their dump:
```
goroutine 2145 [chan receive]:
 net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop(...)
 client/paginator.(*window).Acquire -> blocked
```
yasmin: That sounds like our Go paginator's window semaphore isn't releasing when auth refresh triggers a retry path. JS has a different flow so it avoids the leak.
chris: Repro steps I did: run sample app with pages=50 concurrency=16, set auth token TTL very short so refresh happens mid-run. Go SDK showed degenerate queueing and lower throughput, JS unaffected.
marta: We should check two things: 1) semaphore release on retry/error path in Go paginator, 2) whether our client-side backpressure counts pending retries as active windows. If retries count, then auth refresh can starve new requests.
tom: Quick patch suggestion: when a request is retried due to auth, decrement activeWindow before scheduling retry, or treat retry as separate attempt that re-enters window acquisition. Also add a strict timeout on window acquisition so a stuck goroutine doesn't block forever.
yasmin: I'll open a PR to align Go behavior with JS: re-acquire semantics on retry and a 15s window-acquire timeout with metric emit (client.window.acquire.timeout). We'll also add a unit test that simulates mid-run auth rotation.
chris: Can we add a short blurb in the quickstart about setting auth token TTL to avoid mid-run refresh for onboarding? Might be helpful for customers using short-lived creds.
marta: Also add a note to DX troubleshooting: if you see time-to-first-success > 20s during imports, try lowering concurrency or enable sampleAppPrewarm.
devex-bot: Created RED-DEVEX-1241: go-sdk: paginator window semaphore not released on auth-retry -> add re-acquire semantics + timeout (severity: high).
